subject: Acme AI — unit economics & continuous-batching next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Leah Wong <leah.wong@acme.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:32:00 -0800
Subject: Acme AI discovery: unit econ + batching follow-up

Hi Leah / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and 3 asks so we can turn this into a scoped proposal.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary workload: in-app assistant for customer support and automated summaries. Mixed-session traffic: many short, sub-200-token turns; occasional multi-turn threads up to ~1k tokens.
- Traffic shape: baseline traffic (EST) with predictable 4–6 hour day-time peaks, plus irregular high-volume campaign windows.
- SLA needs: 99.9% availability, p99 latency target ~300ms for short-turn responses.

What we need from you (to finalize unit-econ sketch / sizing)
1) Confirm representative monthly token volume (avg and 95th percentile). You mentioned a pilot at \"low millions/day\" — can you give a realistic month estimate (e.g., 60M tokens/month) and a peak day estimate?
2) Target cost envelope: you gave a rough budget range on the call. Can you confirm target $/1M tokens or monthly budget band (e.g., $X–$Y per month)?
3) Concurrency & latency tolerances during bursts: are spikes allowed to queue (we can autoscale) or do you need strict per-request latency caps that require reserved concurrency?

Attached: acme_pricing_req.pdf (your prior note) — I summarized the items above and added a short set of variables we use for cost modeling.

Next steps we propose once you confirm the items above:
- We’ll produce a 2–3 page economics memo showing: estimated monthly cost, config options (dedicated vs hosted), and batching/concurrency recommendations.
- If the economics fit, schedule a 30-min technical deep dive with our runtime lead to align on KV/prefix caching and expected hit rates.

Thanks — I’ll draft the memo as soon as we get the numbers.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

From: Leah Wong <leah.wong@acme.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme AI discovery: unit econ + batching follow-up

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline below.

1) Token volumes: for pilot (Q4) we expect ~30M tokens/month. Production (Q1) target is 600M tokens/month if the pilot metrics hold; peak day during launch campaigns could approach 35M tokens/day.

2) Budget / $/1M target: our finance/ops target is approximately $25–$35 per 1M tokens (all-in) as an upper bound for hosted inference during evaluation. For long term we’d consider reserved capacity if unit costs drop under $20/1M.

3) Concurrency & latency: we need interactive experience — short-turn responses should generally be <500ms p95. During launch spikes we can accept short (1–3s) tail increases but prefer graceful degradation (quality-preserving fallbacks) rather than long queues. We can discuss small queued bursts but anything >5s is user-visible and undesirable.

Additional notes:
- Traffic mix: ~78% short-turn (30–120 tokens); ~22% long-form (400–1200 tokens) delivered in smaller batches. Streaming answers are required for the short-turns.
- KV/prefix caching: we estimate a 40–60% cache hit for repeated prompts (templates + user context) once warm.

Attaching the procurement packet; Tom will follow up with any contract-specific constraints.

Thanks — Leah
Leah Wong
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme AI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme AI discovery: unit econ + batching follow-up (internal recommendation)

Markus / Monica — forwarding Leah's answers. Quick internal notes and recommended approach so we can turn this into a proposal.

Key variables from Leah:
- Pilot: 30M tokens/mo; Prod: 600M tokens/mo expected.
- Peak day: ~35M tokens/day.
- Target $/1M tokens: $25–$35 (evaluation); < $20 long-term with reserved.
- Traffic: ~78% short-streaming (30–120 tokens), 22% long (400–1200 tokens).
- Cache hit ~45% (midpoint).

Our recommended config (initial proposal):
1) Hosted + burstable dedicated pool during launch: start on hosted API with autoscaling policy tuned for short-turn latency, reserve a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPU pods) for predictable daytime peaks during the pilot launch windows.
2) Batching assumptions: continuous micro-batching for short-turns with target batch windows of 5–12ms to preserve streaming; effective per-GPU concurrency target 40–80 tokens-in-flight for short requests depending on model size.
3) Concurrency & pod sizing: estimate steady-state concurrency ~150 across cluster during normal peak, burst up to 450 for campaign windows. Recommend pod sizing that allows graceful shedding + automatic fallback to smaller model variant for cold overflow.
4) Caching & hit-rate modeling: assume 45% KV/prefix cache hit — that reduces total token compute by ~20–25% in our model. We’ll include scenarios at 30% and 60% to show sensitivity.
5) Cost estimate (very preliminary): using current public model variants, estimate hosted all-in $/1M tokens ~ $28 (mid) for the pilot traffic shape. If they commit to 6–12 month reserved capacity and we enable quantized model variants + optimized kernels, estimate long-term $/1M to drop toward $16–$18.

Attachments planned for external: redwood_estimates_ACME_Q4_v1.pdf and a simple pricing_matrix.xlsx that shows line items and assumptions. I’ll draft the memo and attach these.

Questions for Markus: can you sanity-check the per-GPU concurrency targets and recommended pod counts? Also any immediate optimizations (quant levels / model variants) you’d push for this profile?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme AI — proposed next steps + APM (mutual action plan)

Hi Leah / Tom — attaching a short economics memo (redwood_estimates_ACME_Q4_v1.pdf) and a simple pricing matrix that breaks down assumptions (pricing_matrix.xlsx). Highlights:
- Pilot estimate: ~30M tokens/mo -> estimated hosted cost ~$850 (this is illustrative; see memo for breakdown).
- Production estimate: 600M tokens/mo -> estimated hosted all-in mid $/1M ~ $28 -> monthly ~$16.8k; reserved estimate reduces to ~$10.8k at scale (quantized + reserved).
- Key levers: cache hit rate, batch-window tuning, model quantization profile, and reserved commitment.

Proposed mutual action plan (APM):
1) Procurement: review attached procurement packet and confirm any compliance/KMS requirements (due: Nov 29).
2) Tech deep dive: schedule 45-min runtime session with Markus and Monica to validate cache hit-rate assumptions and sizing (target week of Dec 6).
3) Pilot kickoff: agree on pilot success criteria (token volumes, p95 latency <500ms for short-turns, and user satisfaction metric).
4) Contracting: if pilot aligns, procurement to confirm reserved capacity interest and timeline (we’ll circulate a simple term sheet).

Links: DocuSign term-sheet (draft) — https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123

If this plan looks good, can you confirm by Nov 29 for procurement items and suggest 3 slots for the tech deep dive?

Thanks and happy to iterate on the memo.

Best,
